static_traits.name: Li Chen
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends and family are somewhat strained
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar problems or psychotherapy experience in the past
static_traits.language_features: Calm tone, clear expression, cooperative in exploration; open to systematic recording; overall neutral attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling bored and dissatisfied with my current lifestyle, repeatedly having thoughts like 'no matter what I do I will always be bored'; started months ago, with increased stress over time; spending hours daily on the computer seeking distraction (watching foreign movies and TV shows) but finding it hard to relieve; trying to change routines and start new activities still leaves me dissatisfied, affecting sleep, motivation, work, and interpersonal relationships.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to address boredom and dissatisfaction, improving mental health and overall well-being.

core_beliefs: No matter what I do, I will always be bored, unable to feel satisfied
The problem is with me; I am not suited to feel happy

special_situations.event: Still feeling empty and bored after watching foreign movies and TV shows on the computer for a long time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If even novel content cannot interest me, I will never find satisfaction
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increasing distraction stimuli (continuing to browse the computer, switching content) to fight boredom
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Watching more is useless; I will always be bored.

special_situations.event: After trying new activities (reading new books, walking, photography), enthusiasm fades quickly
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If an activity cannot keep bringing excitement, it is utterly meaningless, and it proves I am not suited for it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Quickly gives up when interest declines and turns to other distractions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I really cannot persist; any activity ends up utterly meaningless.

special_situations.event: When thinking about starting to learn an instrument or joining a sports club
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Since previous attempts brought no change, this time will be no exception
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdrawing or procrastinating before acting to avoid disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will not change anything either; do not waste effort.

special_situations.event: When reflecting on why these activities have not brought satisfaction
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Not feeling satisfied means the problem is with me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-attribution and self-blame, lowers expectations, reduces communication with others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Maybe the problem really is with me; I am destined never to find happiness.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to find lasting interest and satisfaction, to experience vitality and meaning in life
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that no matter what I do nothing will change, feeling disappointed and futile again
defense_goal: Through lowering expectations and distraction, avoids the pain of disappointment
Maintains the status quo; reduces attempts to avoid feelings of failure

object_relations.self_representation: A person who always feels empty and finds it hard to obtain happiness
object_relations.object_representation: Finds it hard to truly understand his family and friends (bystanders expecting him to be 'normally happy')

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing or planning to try new activities (such as learning an instrument)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Views new attempts as 'another doomed failure', and believes others also expect oneself to change quickly
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a supportive, non-confrontational tone, first empathize with their worry about disappointment; then invite them to distinguish facts from predictions, specifying small testable steps and evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes using behavioral experiments and data recording
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Creates distance from emotions by emphasizing 'analysis and rationality', avoiding the pain of being disappointed again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Keeping a gentle and steady tone, inviting them to label emotional intensity and bodily sensations while describing data; using open-ended questioning, encouraging contact with emotions within a safe range.

manifestations: Tried new activities many times but the novelty fades quickly
Spending hours online seeking exploration and distraction yet hard to be satisfied
Relationship tension with family and friends
outcomes: Insufficient motivation to act, and avoidance

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-blame ('it is all my problem')
Before starting, repeatedly worries whether it is 'useful', thus hesitating or holding back

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally meant to be sent outward toward herself, pressing back into herself the impulses that could have sought support or expression outwardly.
manifestations: Not discussing true feelings with friends, turning energy toward self-depletion (prolonged online distraction)
When disappointed, presses the sense of loss in his heart instead of seeking support

positive_force: Having several friends to confide in (though not yet opened up)
Willing to seek professional help and accept a behavioral experiment plan
Has proactively tried various new activities (reading, walking, photography)
Open to systematic recording and analysis
negative_force: Catastrophizing and predicting the future: believing 'I will always be bored'
Overgeneralizing: inferring 'everything is meaningless' from a few fading interests
Self-attribution of blame and negative labels ('there is something wrong with me')
Relieving discomfort with prolonged online distraction, forming a vicious cycle
Withdrawing or procrastinating before starting, reducing opportunities for positive attempts

target_behavior.behavior: Spends long periods online distracted (watching foreign movies / shows)
antecedent: When daily life lacks interest and one needs to 'find some stimulation'
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeking brief novelty and a sense of exploration to relieve boredom and emptiness (believing distraction can bring satisfaction)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome emotional experiences (boredom, emptiness), gaining brief attention shifts and stimulation
target_behavior.consequence: Short-term distraction but long-term greater dissatisfaction; sleep affected, decreased drive, impaired work performance and interpersonal relationships

target_behavior.behavior: Developing negative anticipation and avoiding/procrastinating before starting new activities
antecedent: When thinking about learning an instrument or joining a sports club
Recalls past experiences of 'the novelty wearing off quickly'
target_behavior.core_reason: Negative predictions about the future and fear of being disappointed again ('nothing will change')
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the pain of failure and disappointment in anticipation
target_behavior.consequence: Maintaining a monotonous life and sense of meaninglessness, reducing opportunities for positive experiences, further weakening self-efficacy
